import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type (boxplot)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', ax=axes[0, 0], palette='viridis')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price colored by 4K video capability (scatter plot)
scatter = axes[0, 1].scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], 
                            c=df['has_video_4k'], cmap='coolwarm', 
                            alpha=0.6, s=50, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Megapixels vs Price (Colored by 4K Video Capability)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Create custom legend for 4K capability
legend_elements = [plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#1f77b4', 
                             markersize=10, label='No 4K Video'),
                   plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#d62728', 
                             markersize=10, label='Has 4K Video')]
axes[0, 1].legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper left')

# 3. Camera count by brand (top 10 brands)
brand_counts = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
bars = axes[1, 0].bar(brand_counts.index, brand_counts.values, color=plt.cm.Set3(np.arange(len(brand_counts))))
axes[1, 0].set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Count', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Brand', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[1, 0].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 0.5,
                   f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 4. Weight vs Price by body type (scatter with regression lines)
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
colors = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, len(body_types)))

for body_type, color in zip(body_types, colors):
    subset = df[df['body_type'] == body_type]
    axes[1, 1].scatter(subset['weight_grams'], subset['price_usd'], 
                      color=color, alpha=0.6, s=40, label=body_type, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.3)
    
    # Add regression line
    if len(subset) > 1:
        z = np.polyfit(subset['weight_grams'], subset['price_usd'], 1)
        p = np.poly1d(z)
        x_range = np.linspace(subset['weight_grams'].min(), subset['weight_grams'].max(), 100)
        axes[1, 1].plot(x_range, p(x_range), color=color, alpha=0.8, linewidth=2)

axes[1, 1].set_title('Weight vs Price by Body Type (with Regression Lines)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].legend(title='Body Type', fontsize=9, title_fontsize=10)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
